title: Navier–Stokes SIMS with an active relationship guard
authorization: User requested the Navier–Stokes version with equal and unequal influence and the guard participating throughout.
scope: 2D incompressible periodic fluid coupled to two abstract internal SIMS fields. No material identification or physical second calibration.
initial: psi=sin(x)sin(y)+0.25cos(2x+y)+0.15sin(x-2y); (u,v)=(psi_y,-psi_x). xA=-0.55+0.15cos(x)+0.1sin(y); xB=0.35+0.1sin(x)-0.15cos(y). Guards both 0.5. Same finite trigonometric fields on every grid.

modes.shared: Both guards evolve toward the mean of the two directional sigmoid targets. Exactly equal guards; equal realized gains at equal weights. Explicit modified-rule control.
modes.frozen: Diagnostic: guards fixed at 0.5. SIMS still interact through them; not active-guard evidence.
modes.no_feedback: Diagnostic: directional guards evolve, but viscosity is fixed at its common initial value mu+a. Disables guard-to-flow stress feedback, retaining advection and strain-to-guard.
modes.no_strain: Diagnostic: directional guards evolve with guard-dependent viscosity but chi=0. Disables the explicit strain-to-guard term; advection still couples flow and SIMS/guards.

pulse.sign: positive only in this bounded test

method: Fourier collocation with strict 2/3 truncation for quadratic products, Leray pressure projection, RK4 on velocity, SIMS states and guards together; full divergence of variable symmetric viscous stress. Nonpolynomial reaction resolution is assessed by grid refinement.

independent.method: DOP853 with a separately implemented curl-form momentum equation and conservative scalar transport
independent.cases: directional / all three weights / pulse B

relabel.cases: all nine directional cases; reverse k and pulse recipient, exchange participant baselines and initial states

measurements: Peak sampled spatial RMS change in the unperturbed SIM and fluid velocity, subtracting each case's own no-pulse counterpart. Also guard response, energy, dissipation, momentum, realized-gain differences, full-band field differences at five saved times and control contrasts.
interpretation: Changing weights tests imposed influence while other parameters and total configured weight stay fixed; realized gains are not fixed.
Shared versus directional guards change a response law, not just a weight.
The viscosity closure is a proposed assumption. More transmission increases viscous resistance here; this mapping is not supplied by the original framework.
No mechanical forcing: the guard changes dissipation but supplies no kinetic energy.
All conditions use one chosen smooth spatial initial pattern. A/B relabelings are controls, not independent samples.
No irreversible memory, rupture threshold, molecular chemistry, three-dimensional turbulence or continuum theorem is tested.
Keep every failed screen and failed run. No automatic retries, horizon extension, added cases or changes after freezing.
